nodes.summary: If `Φ` has the restricted isometry property of order `s + s'` with constant `δ`, and `x`, `x'` are supported on disjoint sets `T`, `T'` with `#T ≤ s` and `#T' ≤ s'`, then `|⟪Φ x, Φ x'⟫| ≤ δ ‖x‖₂ ‖x'‖₂`.
nodes.title: Near-orthogonality of disjointly supported sparse vectors

nodes.summary: If `Φ` has the restricted isometry property of order `2 s` with a constant `δ < 1`, then two `s`-sparse vectors `x`, `x'` with `Φ x = Φ x'` are equal.
nodes.title: Uniqueness of sparse solutions under `δ_{2s} < 1`

nodes.summary: Let `s ≥ 1` and let `Φ` have the restricted isometry property of order `2 s` with a constant `δ < √2 - 1`. If `x` is `s`-sparse, then every `xhat` with `Φ xhat = Φ x` and `‖xhat‖₁ ≤ ‖x‖₁` equals `x`; so `x` is the unique solution of `min {‖x̃‖₁ | Φ x̃ = Φ x}`.
nodes.title: Exact recovery of sparse vectors by `ℓ₁` minimization

nodes.summary: If `x` vanishes off `T`, then `x` has at most `#T` nonzero entries.
nodes.title: A vector supported on `T` is `#T`-sparse

nodes.summary: Every `s`-sparse vector `x`, that is every `x` with at most `s` nonzero entries (`hammingNorm x ≤ s`), satisfies `(1 - δ) ‖x‖₂² ≤ ‖Φ x‖₂² ≤ (1 + δ) ‖x‖₂²`.
nodes.title: The restricted isometry property of order `s` with constant `δ`

nodes.summary: The restricted isometry property of order `s` with constant `δ` implies it for every smaller order `s' ≤ s` and every larger constant `δ' ≥ δ`; in particular `δ_{s'} ≤ δ_s`.
nodes.title: Monotonicity of the restricted isometry property

nodes.summary: If `ι` is nonempty, `s ≥ 1` and `Φ` has the restricted isometry property of order `s` with constant `δ`, then `0 ≤ δ` (apply the definition to a standard basis vector).
nodes.title: Isometry constants are nonnegative

nodes.summary: Let `s ≥ 1` and let `Φ` have the restricted isometry property of order `2 s` with a constant `δ < √2 - 1` (that is, `δ_{2s} < √2 - 1`). Then `Φ` has the restricted nullspace property restricted nullspace property over every set `S` of at most `s` indices. Indeed `δ < √2 - 1` is equivalent to `ρ = √2 δ / (1 - δ) < 1`.
nodes.title: Restricted isometry implies the restricted nullspace property

nodes.summary: Let `s ≥ 1` and let `Φ` have the restricted isometry property of order `2 s` with a constant `δ < √2 - 1`. nodes.summary: Let `s ≥ 1` and let `Φ` have the restricted isometry property of order `2 s` with a constant `δ < 1`. For every `h` in the nullspace of `Φ` and every set `T₀` of at most `s` indices, `‖h_{T₀}‖₁ ≤ ρ ‖h_{T₀ᶜ}‖₁` with `ρ = √2 δ / (1 - δ)`.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
